panels.description: Reference for the BLOCKED panels above. Codes are Meta's, as returned on the send that blocked the user.

options.content:
#### Facebook / Meta error codes — what BLOCKED actually means

| code | short | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `10` | outside 24h window | Send attempted after Meta's 24-hour messaging window closed and no message tag applied. |
| `551` | user unreachable | "This person isn't available right now" — account deactivated or otherwise unreachable. |
| `100` | invalid parameter | Meta reuses this for three distinct causes here: missing/unapproved template, malformed send payload, or an attachment_id minted on a different page. |
| `190` | token invalid / expired | Page access token revoked or invalidated. Needs re-provisioning. |
| `200` | missing permission | The app or page token lacks a permission required for the action. |
| `2022` | Messenger rate limit | Messenger-specific send-rate limit. Transient. |
| `613` | app-wide rate limit | Graph API application-level throttle — wider blast radius than 2022. |
| `80006` | page rate limit | Messenger per-page Conversations API limit. |
| `1200` | temporary Meta failure | Meta documents this as transient. Retried in-process 3x, but NOT in DEAN_FB_CODES — once those attempts are spent nothing retries it again. |
| `-1` | undocumented | Not a real Meta code. Present in DEAN_FB_CODES since the earliest git history with no traceable definition; it is retried regardless. |
| `(none)` | never reached Meta | No code came back at all — the page token lookup failed, or the request never completed. These are NOT retryable: fb_error_code is NULL, and NULL = ANY(...) is never true in SQL, so dean's query can never match them. |

*A code appearing here is not by itself a judgement about fault — codes `10`, `190` and `551` are currently treated as expected churn, but that classification is under review. `(none)` and `1200` are the two where nothing will ever retry the user.*

panels.description: The four alerts with no other home: SurveyStuckUsersSpike, SurveyErrorSpike, MultiSurveyErrorRegression, DeanExpiredWaits. These read the study_health collector (1h window, form/study labels, no researcher), which is a different substrate from the rest of this board — so numbers here will NOT tie out against the panels above. Users repeating the same question — the signal for a validation loop or a question people can't answer. Alert SurveyStuckUsersSpike fires at >= 10 per shortcode sustained 20m; the marker sits at that line.

It is fixed at a 1h window and ignores the $window selector, and it carries no researcher label — so the Researcher filter does not apply here. This is the same data the alert rules read, which is the point: what pages you is what you see.

list.description: Which distinct-user window to read. EVERY window is a distinct-user count, not a sum of buckets: 5m = who is here right now, 24h = distinct people we talked to today. 24h is NOT the sum of 288 5m buckets. Single-select on purpose: this metric carries all three windows as separate series, so an 'All' option would sum them and triple-count every number on the board. There is deliberately no way to do that.
list.label: Window
list.name: window

list.description: LEVEL 1 of the hierarchy: the account that owns the survey (users.email). Selecting a researcher narrows the Survey list below it. 'unknown' means the shortcode has no surveys row — those people are still counted, never dropped. Listed from the 24h window so the picker does not empty out on a quiet 5m.
list.label: Researcher
list.name: researcher

list.description: LEVEL 2 of the hierarchy: surveys.survey_name, constrained to the selected Researcher. Resolved from the newest surveys row for the shortcode.
list.label: Survey
list.name: survey

list.description: LEVEL 3 of the hierarchy: surveys.shortcode, constrained to the selected Researcher and Survey. '(none)' means the user had no form resolved yet — usually a platform failure that happened before a form was found, so it is kept, not dropped. To EXCLUDE rather than include, use the Exclude box.
list.label: Shortcode
list.name: shortcode

list.description: Regex of shortcodes to REMOVE, applied as shortcode!~"<value>". Empty = exclude nothing (an empty regex negation is a no-op, so nothing is hidden by default). Type 305 to drop the fallback-target survey, or 305|test for several. This exists because Grafana 7 multi-select can only include, and excluding is the common need — shortcode 305 is both a real live survey and the global fallback target, so it carries most FORM_NOT_FOUND errors. Nothing is excluded anywhere by construction; this box is the only exclusion on either dashboard and it is always visible.
list.label: Exclude shortcodes
list.name: exclude_shortcode

list.description: The messaging page/account carrying the conversation. NOT part of the researcher hierarchy — a page is shared across researchers, so it is an independent cut. This is the axis that separates a channel problem (one page, many surveys) from a survey problem.
list.label: Page
list.name: page_name
